kaḍḍhati: kaḍḍhati [dialect. form supposed to equal Sk. karṣati, cp. Prk. kaḍḍhai to pull, tear, khaḍḍā pit, dug--out. See also Bloomfield, J.A.O.S. XIV. 1921 p. 465.] 1. to draw out, drag, pull, tug J I.193, 225, 265, 273 (khaggaṃ k. to draw the sword). -- 2. to draw in, suck up (udakaṃ) J IV.141. -- 3. to draw a line, to scratch J. I.78, 111, 123; VI.56 (lekhaṃ).
kaḍḍhana: kaḍḍhana (nt.). 1. pulling, drawing Miln 231. <-> 2. refusing, rejecting, renunciation, appl. to the selfdenial of missionary theras following Gotama Buddha"s example Mhvs 12, 55.
